review_candidates.title: Peaks Region Chief Medical Officer
review_candidates.description: Job Description The Regional Chief Medical Officer (RCMO) is a member of the Region Executive Team (RET) and a senior enterprise clinical leader. The RCMO is responsible for ensuring the delivery of high-quality, safe, and efficient care across acute care hospitals, ambulatory delivery assets, and the employed medical group. The RCMO works collaboratively with the region president, region Chief Nursing Officer, hospital administrators, medical directors, and other key stakeholders to align clinical strategy, operations, and performance with Intermountain Health mission, vision, and values. The Region CMO serves as a key leader in advancing our integrated health system's mission, promoting clinical excellence, fostering collaboration and supporting the implementation of Value Based Care initiatives. The individual in this position must reside in the Peaks Region. Essential Functions Provides clinical oversight and direction for the region, ensuring compliance with regulatory, accreditation, and quality standards. Leads the development and implementation of clinical services, policies, and initiatives that support the region's strategic goals and objectives. Supports and champions clinical and strategic growth across the region including growth in Proactive Care and Children’s Health. Serves as liaison to Clinical Excellence Committee of the Region Board. Champions the adoption and integration of evidence-based practices, clinical protocols, and best practices across the region in close collaboration with Intermountain Health Clinical Programs. Supports the recruitment, retention, development, and engagement of physicians and advanced practice professionals in the region. Develops and nurtures collaborative relationships with independent and affiliate physicians and APPs across markets and regions. Fosters a culture of collaboration, communication, and accountability among the clinical leaders and staff in the region. Represents the region's clinical interests and perspectives in enterprise-level decision making and planning. Builds and maintains effective relationships with internal and external partners, including community organizations, academic institutions, and other health care entities. Advocates for the needs and interests of the patients, families, and communities served by the region. Participates in ongoing professional development and education activities to maintain and enhance clinical expertise and leadership skills. Drives clinical integration and collaboration across the region and the enterprise, leveraging the Intermountain Operating Model and the clinical governance structure. Develops and empowers strong teams of clinical leaders who can effectively manage the clinical operations and performance of the region. Works collaboratively with nursing and enterprise clinical and non-clinical shared services to optimize the delivery of care and the use of resources. Qualifications MD or DO degree from an accredited medical school. Board certification in a clinical specialty recognized by the American Board of Medical Specialties or the American Osteopathic Association. Current and unrestricted license to practice medicine in the state of Colorado, Montana, Nevada, or Utah or eligible to obtain one. Minimum of 10 years of clinical experience and 5 years of progressive leadership experience in a health care organization. Demonstrated knowledge and skills in clinical quality improvement, patient safety, population health, and health care delivery systems. Excellent communication, interpersonal, and influencing skills. Strong strategic thinking, problem-solving, and decision-making abilities. High degree of integrity, professionalism, and ethical behavior. Commitment to the Intermountain Health mission, vision, and values. This is an exempt, full-time position with a compensation range of $504,025 - $597,613, annually, and as determined by prior years of relevant experience. With this position, you are eligible to participate in the Annual Pay for Performance (AP4P) Plan. This plan enables Intermountain Health to provide leaders with an additional performance compensation opportunity. The AP4P award opportunities are calculated as a percentage of your base salary. Awards are paid out based on attainment of selected Board-approved goals. Location: Peaks Regional Office Work City Broomfield Work State Colorado Scheduled Weekly Hours 40 The hourly range for this position is listed below. Actual hourly rate dependent upon experience. $70.00 - $450.00 We care about your well-being – mind, body, and spirit – which is why we provide our caregivers a generous benefits package that covers a wide range of programs to foster a sustainable culture of wellness that encompasses living healthy, happy, secure, connected, and engaged. Learn More About Our Comprehensive Benefits Package Here. By applying for a position with Intermountain, I acknowledge that I will comply with all applicable Intermountain policies and expectations. If applying for a remote or hybrid role, this includes remote work expectations related to confidentiality, information security, work schedules, conflicts of interest, and use of company equipment. I further acknowledge that outside employment or activities may not interfere with job responsibilities or create a conflict of interest with Intermountain. Actual or reasonably perceived conflicts may be grounds for disqualification from consideration or, if hired, corrective action up to and including termination of employment. Intermountain Health is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, age, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or protected veteran status. At Intermountain Health, we use the artificial intelligence ("AI") platform, HiredScore to improve your job application experience. While HiredScore assists in reviewing applications, all final decisions are made by Intermountain personnel to ensure fairness. We protect your privacy and follow strict data protection rules. Title: Payroll & Accounts Officer Location: Ortigas, Pasig, PH Work Schedule: Monday to Friday, 6:00 AM to 3:00 PM PH Time (Full Onsite) Position Summary The client is seeking a detail-oriented Payroll & Accounts Officer to support payroll processing and day-to-day accounting operations across its retail stores. The role will be responsible for ensuring accurate and timely payroll, maintaining compliance with Australian payroll requirements, processing accounts payable, and completing daily bank reconciliations. The ideal candidate has at least two years of Australian payroll and accounting experience, is proficient in Xero, and has a sound understanding of Australian awards and payroll compliance requirements. Key Responsibilities 1. Payroll Processing Process weekly payroll for retail store employees, integrating timesheet data from Tanda into Xero. Review timesheets, leave applications, employee records, and new starter documentation to ensure payroll accuracy. Ensure compliance with applicable Australian Modern Awards, PAYG withholding tax, superannuation, and other statutory requirements. Prepare payroll bank files and distribute payslips accurately and on time. Prepare weekly and monthly wage reports for store managers, highlighting relevant payroll costs and variances. 2. Accounts Payable Process supplier invoices for retail stores, ensuring accuracy, proper coding, and timely payment. Reconcile supplier statements and investigate outstanding balances and discrepancies. Prepare payment batches in accordance with approved payment schedules and internal controls. Liaise with suppliers and internal stakeholders to resolve invoice and payment queries. 3. Bank Reconciliation Perform daily bank reconciliations to ensure transactions are accurately recorded in Xero. Investigate and resolve unreconciled transactions, discrepancies, and outstanding items promptly. Maintain accurate and up-to-date financial records to support month-end reporting and financial controls. Qualifications and Experience At least 2 years of Australian work experience in payroll processing, accounts payable, and bank reconciliations. Hands-on experience using Xero; experience with Tanda is highly desirable. Working knowledge of Australian Modern Awards, PAYG withholding, superannuation, and payroll compliance requirements. Experience processing weekly payroll and handling employee timesheets and leave records. Strong understanding of accounts payable processes, supplier reconciliations, and bank reconciliations. Excellent attention to detail, numerical accuracy, and organisational skills. Ability to work independently, manage recurring deadlines, and handle confidential payroll and financial information. Key Success Indicators Payroll is processed accurately and on time each week. Payroll records comply with applicable Australian employment and statutory requirements. Supplier invoices and payment batches are processed accurately and within agreed timelines. Daily bank reconciliations are completed promptly, with discrepancies investigated and resolved. Weekly and monthly wage reports are accurate, timely, and useful to store managers.

review_candidates.description: About the Role The Operations Manager, Global Strategic Accounts oversees the day-to-day delivery of a large global enterprise account. This full-time role manages a distributed team of Wellbeing Coordinators and directs the work of contract Health Coaches assigned to the account. Working remotely in the United States, the Operations Manager enables coordinators and coaches to execute campaigns, live sessions, and other program activities across global regions. This role establishes clear expectations, resolves operational issues, and maintains consistent quality while accommodating local needs. The Operations Manager partners closely with the Program Manager on delivery plans and capacity, the Account Director on account priorities and escalations, and the Director of Coaching Operations on coaching standards and quality. While the Program Manager owns program scope and delivery timelines, the Operations Manager owns delivery execution, staffing assignments, and team capacity. Key Responsibilities Lead the global delivery team by hiring, onboarding, managing, and developing Wellbeing Coordinators, establishing clear expectations, providing regular feedback, and addressing performance concerns. Direct contract coaches day-to-day by setting program goals, defining success metrics, providing clear guidance on live events, and aligning coach activities with account strategy. Assign and schedule coaches across one-on-one coaching, live sessions, and fitness classes. Conduct regular team meetings and individual check-ins with coordinators and coaches. Manage workloads, coverage, and areas of specialty across multiple regions and time zones. Establish and uphold delivery standards for how events, outreach, and results are scheduled, tracked, and reported across all regions. Oversee the execution of campaigns, webinars, events, employee communications, coaching, and community activities. Translate program roadmaps into regional delivery plans, operational priorities, and measurable goals. Develop and maintain templates, checklists, playbooks, and operating procedures used by coordinators to prepare and run scheduled activities. Track team availability, coaching utilization, and upcoming delivery commitments to support capacity planning. Record delivered activities against contracted commitments and provide operational data for client reviews. Monitor regional performance across activity types, determine regional programming mix within the roadmap, and recommend roadmap adjustments when appropriate. Maintain operational trackers and coordinate access to internal and client systems with IT and Security teams. Manage day-to-day relationships and budgets for coaching vendors and contractors in partnership with People and Legal teams, ensuring work remains within contracted scope. Monitor service quality, participant feedback, and operational metrics, collaborating with internal leadership to resolve recurring issues and enhance delivery workflows. Exercise decision rights over coach and coordinator assignments, scheduling, regional programming mix, and delivery process changes, while escalating scope, budget, or headcount changes to the Account Director. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree from an accredited college or university. 5+ years of experience in program or service delivery operations. 3+ years of direct people management experience. Ability to consistently work hours that overlap with EMEA and APAC teams. Proven experience leading and developing a distributed team across multiple regions and time zones. Demonstrated experience overseeing ongoing client programs involving multiple activities, stakeholders, and delivery commitments. Experience coordinating contractors or specialized service providers while managing team coverage and capacity. Demonstrated ability to develop clear delivery processes, quality standards, and escalation paths. Experience using service data and participant feedback to resolve operational challenges and improve delivery performance. Compensation and Benefits Expected base salary range: $130,000 - $160,000 per year, dependent on factors such as experience and expertise. Eligibility for performance bonus and equity. Comprehensive health coverage, including medical, dental, and vision insurance. 401(k) retirement plan with organization match. Paid time off. review_candidates.description: Imagine yourself... Doing meaningful work that makes an everyday impact on the world around you. Videojet technologies play a critical role in ensuring the safety and authenticity of products sold across the globe in the food, beverage, pharmaceutical, and industrial marketplaces. As part of the Videojet team and the broader Veralto network, you'll work with products that make an everyday impact on the world around you - and along the way, you'll have opportunities to make your mark on our business and your career with ongoing opportunities to deepen your skillset and pursue your ambitions. Learn about our leading portfolio of innovative products here! Partnering closely with the Sr. Director, Ops Finance the Latin America Regional Operations Finance Manager will serve as a strategic financial business partner for Videojet's Brazil facility and the broader LATAM region. The role will translate financial data into actionable business intelligence, identify productivity opportunities, influence operational decisions, and deliver measurable, favorable cost impacts across Latin America manufacturing operations. The position is based in São Paulo or Extrema, MG, and is hybrid. In this role, a typical day will look like: Lead the development of site-level operating budgets and financial forecasts in partnership with plant leadership. Partner with the Sr Director and regional operations leaders to provide proactive insights that strengthen productivity, cost discipline, and decision-making. Analyze material, labor, and overhead variances and turn findings into clear recommendations for operations leaders. Drive the identification and tracking of cost improvement and productivity initiatives, ensuring financial impacts are quantified, reported, and realized. Deliver monthly regional and site financial reporting, including variance analysis, KPI dashboards, and forward-looking risk and opportunity assessments. Collaborate with global finance and cost accounting teams on consistent costing practices, capital expenditure analysis, close activities, internal controls, audit readiness, and compliance. The essential requirements of the job include: 5-10 years of experience in operations finance, plant controlling, or manufacturing finance within an industrial or manufacturing environment. Bachelor's degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field. Proven experience partnering with operational leaders to identify and deliver cost improvement or productivity outcomes. Experience with ERP systems such as SAP, Oracle, or an equivalent platform, plus strong Microsoft Excel and financial reporting capability. Ability to synthesize complex financial data into clear business narratives for non-finance audiences. Fluency in Portuguese and English, with the ability to communicate effectively across cultures and geographies. Preferred qualifications include: CPA, CRC, or an equivalent professional accounting designation, or active pursuit of one. Experience supporting manufacturing operations within a multinational, publicly traded company. Background in standard costing, inventory management, or manufacturing variance analysis. Familiarity with Brazilian fiscal and tax regulations relevant to manufacturing operations. Familiarity with Lean or continuous improvement methodologies such as Kaizen or VPS. Experience using Power BI or Tableau to develop plant-level financial dashboards. Videojet is proud to be part of the Product Quality & Innovation segment of Veralto (NYSE: VLTO), a $5B global leader dedicated to ensuring access to clean water, safe food and medicine, and trusted essential goods. When you join Veralto's vibrant global network of 17,000 associates, you join a unique culture and work environment where purpose meets possibility : where the work you do has an everyday impact on the resources and essentials we all rely on, and where you'll have valuable opportunities to deepen your skillset, pursue your ambitions, and grow your career. At Veralto, we value diversity and the existence of similarities and differences, both visible and not, found in our workforce, workplace and throughout the markets we serve. Our associates, customers and shareholders contribute unique and different perspectives as a result of these diverse attributes. review_candidates.title: Global Supply Manager - Mechanicals
review_candidates.description: About Supply Chain Resources Group (SCRG) Supply Chain Resources Group (SCRG) is the execution partner for the world's most innovative hardware companies. We help everyone from the biggest tech companies to the most promising start-ups design, implement, and manage their product manufacturing supply chain. SCRG provides manufacturing and supply chain advisory services, vendor management services, and highly skilled technical resources in the world's major manufacturing centers. From prototypes and early-stage New Product Introduction (NPI) to full high volume mass production, our teams bring speed, clarity, and control to complex global supply chains. Role Overview As a Global Supply Manager (GSM) for Mechanicals , you will advise and assist our clients—ranging from industry-leading OEMs to fast-growing hardware startups—with end-to-end commercial and strategic relationships with global mechanical suppliers. You will serve as the commercial leader for the mechanical commodity, responsible for sourcing, negotiating, and scaling precision custom mechanical parts and their tooling, including mechanical and electromechanical sub-assemblies, injection-molded parts, CNC-machined components, die castings, metal extrusions, precision metal stamping and forming, composites, and fasteners. You will bridge the gap between our client's hardware engineering teams and the global supply base, ensuring that custom mechanical components meet rigorous targets for cost, quality, and delivery. You will also help clients build and improve the sourcing processes and tools that support their supply chain. Key Responsibilities Commodity Strategy & Roadmaps: Develop clear technology and commodity roadmaps for current and future programs. Monitor market conditions and supplier technology roadmaps, and identify supply and demand challenges and opportunities. Strategic Sourcing & Supplier Selection: Identify, evaluate, and onboard global suppliers with the right technologies and capabilities. Own the RFI/RFP/RFQ process, review, and business award decisions, ensuring all commercial terms are agreed and documented, and execute supplier capability audits alongside engineering and quality teams. Cost Management & Negotiation: Develop bottom-up "should-cost" models for custom mechanical parts and tooling. Analyze current spend, consolidate volume across the supply base to create leverage, develop sourcing alternatives, and negotiate pricing, Master Supply Agreements (MSAs), Statements of Work (SOWs), and supplier terms to drive cost reductions throughout the product lifecycle. New Product Introduction (NPI) & Early Supplier Involvement: Serve as the liaison between supply chain and engineering for supplier and component selection during NPI and sustaining projects. Facilitate Early Supplier Involvement (ESI) during the DFM (Design for Manufacturing) phase to align part design, materials, and surface finishes with supplier capabilities and cost targets. Tooling, Capacity & Risk Management: Manage custom tooling investments, tooling unit cost targets, and tooling and supplier capacity. Maintain commodity consumption forecasts and execution plans, and develop dual-sourcing strategies to mitigate geopolitical and supply chain risks. Supplier Performance Management: Define and manage supplier performance metrics for technology, quality, supply, and cost. Conduct regular Quarterly Business Reviews (QBRs), drive continuous improvement in yield, cycle time, and on-time delivery (OTD), and lead dispute resolution when needed. Financial Planning Support: Work with client finance teams during monthly close and financial planning cycles on component pricing, cost forecasts, and tooling investments. Cross-Functional Execution: Act as the primary liaison between the client OEM and the contract manufacturers/Tier-2 suppliers, resolving critical path escalations and ensuring smooth transitions from prototype builds (EVT/DVT) to Mass Production (MP). Required Qualifications Experience: 5+ years of experience in global supply management, strategic sourcing, or procurement of custom mechanical components, within hardware, consumer electronics, robotics, aerospace, or related industries. Commodity Expertise: Deep technical and commercial understanding of precision mechanical manufacturing processes, including injection molding and LSR molding, CNC machining, die casting, metal extrusion, precision metal stamping and forming, composites, fasteners, and mechanical and electromechanical sub-assemblies. Surface Treatments: Technical and commercial experience with surface treatments and coatings for plastics and metals, including corrosion-resistant, decorative, and RF-performance coatings. Commercial Acumen: Proven track record of directing complex negotiations, cost/price analysis, RFP/RFQ reviews, and business award processes; structuring supplier contracts, T&Cs, MSAs, SOWs, and NDAs; managing multi-million-dollar spend portfolios; and negotiating capital expenditure (CapEx) for custom tooling. Tooling & Capacity: Experience with tooling capacity management, tooling unit cost targets, and supplier capacity management. Analytical Skills: Experience using should-cost models to set cost targets and negotiate pricing, and the ability to prepare and present quantitative and qualitative comparisons of sourcing alternatives. Global Execution: Extensive experience collaborating with contract manufacturers (CMs) and Tier-2 component suppliers across Greater China and other global manufacturing hubs. Professional Skills: Excellent written and verbal communication, strong ethics and professionalism, and a detail- and team-oriented approach, with the flexibility to deliver in a fast-paced environment and adapt to changing circumstances. Education: Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Materials Science, or a related discipline. Fluency in English and Spanish required to effectively interface between international clients and regional suppliers. Preferred Qualifications Advanced degree (Master's in Engineering, Supply Chain Management or MBA) Experience developing or improving supply chain and sourcing processes and tools. Interest in emerging technologies across consumer electronics, aerospace, and robotics, and in new and developing mechanical manufacturing processes and materials. Experience operating in an embedded-client environment or delivering integrated supply chain solutions.
